adds.title: Constitutional Court of Suriname - February 2023 ruling
adds.summary: On 31 January 2023 the Constitutional Court held the Civil Code to be very outdated, not keeping pace with contemporary developments and urgently requiring amendment, and in the referenced transgender Yvanna precedent the Hof van Justitie had ordered the State/CBB to amend her identity in the public population registers after a gender change completed abroad because outdated legislation could not justify violating her human rights.

adds.title: Eerste Kantongerecht (Court of First Instance) - January 2017 ruling
adds.summary: On 11 January 2017 the Kantongerecht in the Eerste Kanton granted a post-operative trans woman who underwent male-to-female surgery on 22 April 2009 and had obtained a forename change on 12 January 2011 an order changing her legal sex registration from male to female, holding that the contradiction between socio-psychological gender role and birth-certificate registration violated the right to respect for private life under Article 17 Constitution, Article 17 ICCPR and Article 11 ACHR, and, finding Suriname law provides no statutory procedure for transsexual gender-marker change, broadly interpreted Articles 17 and 64-67a Civil Code under Articles 106 and 137 Constitution to order the civil registrar to add a marginal note recording her as belonging to the female sex.
